newsitem.title: USA: MicroEnergy sees revenue growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: MicroEnergy sees revenue growth in 1997.

text.p: MicroEnergy Inc said Wednesday it expects revenues to grow by between 18 percent and 25 percent in the 1997 fiscal year.
Revenues for the 1996 fiscal year, ended June 30, were $14.38 million, slightly lower than the $14.48 registered for the 1995 fiscal year.
"Fiscal 1996 was a pivotal year in the transition for the company," MicroEnergy President and Chief Executive Robert Gatza said in a statement.
The company completed an initial public offering in July, injecting about $2.7 million in net proceeds.

"MicroEnergy has never been in a stronger financial position in the entire 12-year history of our company," Gatza added. "We expect to realize approximately 18 percent to 25 percent revenue growth during fiscal 1997."
MicroEnergy manufactures and markets custom power supplies.
